design: Selected components (PO decision point 1): Temporal server 1.32.1 with its own PostgreSQL for BA-05; SeaweedFS 4.51 for BA-06; TerminusDB 12.0.7-noroot for BA-01 is already a digest-pinned, typed-verified service of the stack (OCOR-DEV-0073) and is unchanged by this change set.

Temporal runs as three containers: temporal-postgresql (the locked postgres image, never published on the host, tmpfs), temporal-admin-tools (official image; applies the pinned PostgreSQL v12 schema with temporal-sql-tool for the temporal and temporal_visibility databases, then keeps the official CLI for probes; healthy only after the strict versioned update succeeds) and temporal (official server image configured by its embedded env template, persistence postgres12, an empty versioned dynamic-config file mounted read-only, frontend published only on 127.0.0.1:17233; it starts only after admin-tools is healthy).

SeaweedFS runs in single-node mini mode on tmpfs; only the S3 gateway is published, on 127.0.0.1:18333. The S3 admin identity is the fixed key id ocor-bootstrap-s3 with the generated disposable secret OCOR_LOCAL_SEAWEEDFS_PASSWORD; unsigned and wrong-secret requests are denied.

Same treatment as the existing services (PO point 4.a): digest pin in infra/services.lock.json and Compose; shared policy (restart no, init, no-new-privileges, dedicated network); memory/CPU limits; health checks; typed verification through dedicated fail-closed qualification modules (deploy/bootstrap/services/temporal and seaweedfs) driven by scripts/verify_external_services.py; bounded pause/unpause/restart fault recovery in the modules; reset unchanged because nothing new is initialised; teardown through the Compose project with zero residue.

CI: scripts/bootstrap_ci_environment.py pulls every locked image and starts the whole Compose profile, so the CI stack gains the four containers without any workflow change; the campaign guard now requires the 15 Compose services as mandatory containers (MANDATORY_CONTAINERS, bound by a test to the Compose profile).

Generated secrets: two new disposable passwords, named with the PASSWORD suffix so the CI diagnostics redaction covers them; an existing env file gains only the missing keys (idempotent, values never rewritten, mode 0600).

Object Lock probe (under --execute): a uniquely named bucket created with Object Lock reports versioning Enabled and ObjectLockEnabled Enabled; one object under COMPLIANCE retention; deleting that version is denied with and without x-amz-bypass-governance-retention; the version stays intact. The probe never deletes the locked version or bucket.

normative_interpretations: Change set a covers server provisioning only. The Python clients named by PO decision point 3 (Temporal, S3, TerminusDB) are adapter dependencies and enter with change sets b, c and d, each under the same dependency policy; adding them here would add unused dependencies to the runtime lock.

DEP-011 (Temporal/PostgreSQL candidate subject to licence verification and benchmark): the licence is verified here (MIT, admitted). The benchmark needs a workflow worker, i.e. the Temporal Python SDK of change set b; it is recorded NOT_EXECUTED here and is carried as an obligation of OCOR-DEV-REM-0039 (adapter Temporal of C6), not claimed.

Object Lock retention mode used by the provisioning probe: COMPLIANCE, because no request, the governance-bypass header included, may shorten or remove it, so the probe proves the strongest fail-closed behaviour; the mode used by the C7 adapter is chosen and motivated in change set c, as PO decision point 1 requires. The probe never uses the bypass to delete: it sends the bypass header only as a negative probe that must be denied.

TerminusDB is part of the decision's provisioning list but is already provisioned and qualified (OCOR-DEV-0073, typed-verified in every bootstrap); the requalification of OCOR-DEV-0073 on the 15-container stack is its provisioning evidence in this change set.

Temporal frontend authentication: the disposable bootstrap runs without an authorizer (TEMPORAL_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=true, loopback-only publication), as the non-production local profile of the other services does; authorisation of workflow operations is a C6 adapter concern (change set b). Recorded as a residual risk, not a claim.

An inventory miss is declared: scripts/run_qualifying_campaign.py hard-coded 11 mandatory containers and was found by the first full-suite attempt (stopped before any test, non-qualifying); it was fixed in this change set and bound by a test, and the whole campaign was re-run at the corrected code commit.

A pre-push run of the inline supply-chain scanner (required check supply-chain) found the AKIA-shaped key id of the published AWS SigV4 example in the SeaweedFS unit contract. The scanner is unchanged; the key id, which is not part of the string to sign, was replaced by a neutral one in 36e6151, the published signature is still asserted, and the whole campaign passed at b81630a was re-run at 36e6151 (non-qualifying attempt a6).

Full serial suite at 36e6151: 4113.5 s (68.6 min), above the 60-minute notification (campaign_result po_decision_required true) and below the 75-minute cap by more than 5 minutes; under REM-0033-LOCAL-FULL-DURATION (2026-10-25) point 4 it is recorded here and in the iteration log without a new decision request. The superseded run at b81630a on the same host and stack took 3431.6 s; the difference is observed, not explained, and no limit was changed.

residual_risks: Infrastructure evidence only: the components exist as real, pinned, fail-closed services; no adapter, no BA conformance (OCOR-DEV-0060), no runtime conformance.
Temporal frontend has no authorizer in the disposable profile (loopback only); SeaweedFS filer IAM gRPC is unauthenticated inside the private Compose network (not published).
No image vulnerability scan was executed: no image scanner is in the toolchain or qualification locks (same situation as the eleven existing service images); recorded NOT_EXECUTED.
tmpfs state: a SeaweedFS restart discards buckets and objects by design; Object Lock persistence across restarts is out of scope of a disposable stack.
CI memory/time: the four containers add about 0.4 GiB at rest locally; the 30-minute main job cap is unchanged and is observed by the CI run of the PR.
